purpose: This medicine is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is used along with diet and exercise to keep your blood sugar in a healthy range. It combines two different medicines in one pill to make it easier to manage your diabetes.
how_it_works: Metformin works by reducing the amount of sugar your liver releases into your blood and helps your body use insulin more effectively. Pioglitazone helps your muscle and fat cells respond better to insulin, so sugar can move out of your blood and into your cells where it belongs. Together, these two medicines tackle blood sugar from two different angles, giving you better control.
common_side_effects: Upset stomach, nausea, diarrhea, or a metallic taste in your mouth, especially when you first start taking it. You may also notice some weight gain or mild swelling in your hands or feet. These effects often improve after the first few weeks.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you notice unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing, stomach pain, or feel very tired, as these can be rare signs of a serious condition called lactic acidosis. This medicine can increase the risk of bone fractures, especially in women, and may increase the risk of bladder cancer with long-term use. Do not take it if you have kidney problems, heart failure, or liver disease. You should stop taking it before any surgery or procedures using contrast dye.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is one tablet taken once or twice a day with meals to reduce stomach upset. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on how well your blood sugar is controlled. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose without talking to them first.
